name: Ngoloko
body:
NGOLOKO
CR 5

This brown-furred predator has a broad, bear-like body with forelegs longer than its hind legs, and oversized jaws for its head.

XP 1,600
N Large animal
Init +5; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +9

DEFENSE

AC 17, touch 10, flat-footed 16 (+1 Dex, +7 natural, –1 size)
hp 67 (9d8+27)
Fort +9, Ref +7, Will +6

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee 2 claws +11 (1d8+5), bite +10 (2d6+5 plus grab)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks pounce

STATISTICS

Str 21, Dex 12, Con 16, Int 2, Wis 13, Cha 14
Base Atk +6; CMB +12 (+16 grapple); CMD 23 (27 vs. trip)
Feats Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Power Attack, Vital Strike, Weapon Focus (claw)
Skills Acrobatics +6 (+10 to jump), Climb +10, Perception +9
SQ hold breath

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Crippling Claw (Ex)

The ngoloko gains a +4 bonus on critical hit confirmation rolls with its claws, and on a confirmed critical hit agathe target is stunned 1d4 rounds (DC 19 Fortitude partial); creatures that successfully save are staggered for 1 round instead. If the ngoloko hits a stunned creature with its claw (even if not a critical hit), the target is knocked unconscious for 1d4 rounds (DC 19 Fort negates). The save DC is Strength-based.

Eat Brain (Ex)

As a full-round action, the ngoloko can devour the brain of a dying creature, killing it instantly. Humanoids within 30 feet witnessing the carnage are frightened for 1 round and shaken for 1d6 rounds (DC 16 Will negates). The save DC is Charisma-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm forests
Organization solitary or pair
Treasure none

The ngoloko (also known as kerit) is a powerful forest-dwelling carnivore. While no more evil than any other predatory animal, but they have a reputation for cruelty and malice due to their particular fondness for eating brains and their habit of cracking open the skulls of their victims to devour the tasty gray matter within. This grotesque dietary peculiarity has led to the ngoloko’s fell reputation among humanoids.

Ngolokos are generally solitary, but occasionally mated pairs are encountered. When cubs are born, however, the male usually devours the cub before it can grow to rival and challenge its parent. Mated ngolokos may battle for the life of the cub, even orphaning it if both parents are mortally wounded.
